listenings.text: Hi Renato, it's Dana. I know you're in your tent now, and I know you're nervous. That's normal. Listen. You've had such a good month. Your fitness is so much better, and your strategy is clear. Tonight, don't watch videos and don't read the comments. Have an early night. Before you sleep, close your eyes and visualize your first wave: you paddle, you stand up, you take the drop. Set your alarm for five thirty. Your heat is at eight, so we've got plenty of time. You're ready, mate. See you at the tent at seven.

Hey mate, it's Kai. I'm in the tent next to yours, but I don't want to wake Tom, so I'm sending a message. What a day! The drive was so long, but the scenery was amazing, and that sunset at the beach was so beautiful. Okay, the plan for tomorrow. Breakfast is at six, in the van. Jess is bringing bananas and toast. We leave the campsite at six forty, because the parking lot gets so crowded. And don't forget your jersey number. You're number four. Get some sleep!

paras: Friday, 9:30 p.m. I'm writing this in my tent at the campsite in Prevelly. The semifinal is tomorrow morning, and I can't sleep. I feel so restless.

We left Perth at noon in the club van. It was such a long drive: almost four hours, with one rest stop. But the scenery was so beautiful. There were green hills, old trees and even kangaroos next to the road. Kai played such loud music that Tom put his hoodie over his ears.

We arrived at five, just in time for the sunset. It was such an amazing sunset, orange and pink over the water. Then Dana gave us a pep talk next to the van. She was so calm, and her words were so simple: "Trust your plan. Enjoy your waves."

The people at the campsite are such nice people. A family from Busselton gave us hot chocolate. Now everybody is asleep, except me. My alarm is set for 5:30. I'm going to close my eyes, visualize my first wave and try to have an early night. Well, not so early now!
